note.explanation: Time complexity describes how an algorithm’s running time changes as the input gets bigger. Space complexity describes how much memory it uses. Dry runs and simulations help check that an algorithm works as intended.
examples: If you check each name in a list one by one, a longer list may take more steps.
A dry run uses sample data to check an algorithm without actually running a program.
note.checkAnswer: A dry run is a manual check of an algorithm using sample data.
note.simple: Time complexity is about time and steps; space complexity is about memory. A dry run is a careful test using sample data.

example.question: Think of a simple task, like finding the largest number in a list. Write down the steps you would take to complete this task. Now, imagine the list has 10 numbers, then 100 numbers. How do the steps change?
example.answer: To find the largest number, keep the first number as the largest so far, compare each remaining number with it, and update the largest when a bigger number is found. A list of 100 numbers requires more comparisons than a list of 10 numbers.

explain.title: Time complexity
explain.body: Time Complexity measures how fast or slow an algorithm performs. It shows how the running time of an algorithm changes as the size of the input increases. For example, finding a name may take longer in a list of 1,000 names than in a list of 10 names.

explain.title: Big O notation
explain.body: Time complexity is usually expressed using Big O notation, like O(n), O(logn), or O(n²). It helps compare algorithms to see which one is faster.

explain.title: Space complexity
explain.body: Space complexity measures the amount of memory an algorithm uses relative to input size. It is essential to consider both the memory required for the input and any extra memory used by the algorithm.

explain.title: Dry runs and simulations
explain.body: Designing and evaluating algorithms involves activities like dry runs and simulations to ensure they work as intended. A dry run follows the algorithm using sample data so you can check its steps and result.

mistakes: Do not confuse time complexity, which is about running time, with space complexity, which is about memory.
Do not define time complexity only as the time for one particular input; it describes how running time changes as input size increases.
Do not say that a dry run means writing or executing program code; describe manually tracing the steps with sample data.
When explaining a dry run’s purpose, include checking the result and finding errors.
